# JVM-Tools (SJK) Analysis of JMH Project

## Overview
This document summarizes the analysis of the **JMH (Java Microbenchmark Harness)** project using **jvm-tools (SJK - Swiss Java Knife)**.

## Tools Used
- **jvm-tools (SJK)**: Built from https://github.com/aragozin/jvm-tools (version 0.24-SNAPSHOT)
- **JMH**: Built from https://github.com/openjdk/jmh (version 1.38-SNAPSHOT)

## Analysis Methodology
1. Built jvm-tools from source using Maven (with toolchain disabled for JDK 17 compatibility)
2. Built JMH project from source using Maven
3. Launched a JMH benchmark (BlackholeBench.explicit_int) with 4 threads, 1000 iterations of 30s each

5. Collected multiple types of diagnostic data

### 1. jps - Java Process Listing
- Listed all JVM processes on the system
- Identified JMH parent process and forked benchmark process

- **Key finding**: 4 JMH worker threads each consuming ~100% CPU
- Total process CPU: ~407% (4 cores fully utilized)
- Worker threads: `org.openjdk.jmh.benchmarks.BlackholeBench.explicit_int-jmh-worker-{1,2,3,4}`
- Allocation rate: 0 b/s to ~600kb/s per worker (compiler blackhole mode)

### 3. hh - Heap Histogram
- Showed JMH infrastructure objects in heap
- Key objects: Blackhole, ThreadParams, InfraControl, BenchmarkParams
- Total of ~60+ JMH-related object types

### 4. gc - GC Information
- G1 Young Generation: 2 collections, 25ms total
- G1 Old Generation: 0 collections
- Very low GC pressure (benchmark uses compiler blackholes)

### 5. stcap - Stack Trace Capture
- Captured 210 stack trace samples at 10ms intervals
- Stored in binary format for analysis

### 6. ssa - Stack Sample Analyzer
- **Thread Info**: 15 threads, 4 JMH workers at ~75% CPU each
- **Frame Histogram**: Most frequent frames are in JMH benchmark stub methods
- **Print**: Full stack traces showing JMH execution path
- **Flame Graph**: Generated SVG flame graph visualization

### 7. vminfo - VM Information
- **System Properties**: JDK 17.0.19, OpenJDK 64-Bit Server VM
- **XX Flags**: Full list of JVM flags (G1GC, tiered compilation, etc.)
- **Perf Counters**: Not available due to module access restrictions on JDK 17

### 8. mx - MBean Operations
- **Memory**: Heap usage 100MB used / 2GB committed / 30GB max
- **Threading**: 21-30 active threads
- **Runtime**: JVM arguments showing JMH-specific flags
- **GC**: G1 Young (2 collections, 25ms), G1 Old (0 collections)
- **ClassLoading**: 2379 loaded classes, 0 unloaded
- **Compilation**: 4229ms total compilation time
- **OS**: 288 available processors, low CPU load

## Key Findings
1. JMH benchmark efficiently utilizes all 4 worker threads at ~100% CPU each
2. Minimal GC pressure with G1GC - only 2 young generation collections
3. Stack traces show the benchmark execution path through JMH infrastructure
4. Heap is well under capacity with only ~100MB used
5. The benchmark uses compiler blackholes to prevent dead code elimination

## Output Files
- `sjk-ttop-output.txt` - Thread CPU monitoring data
- `sjk-hh-output.txt` - Heap histogram
- `sjk-gc-output.txt` - GC information
- `sjk-stcap-output.txt` - Stack capture log
- `jmh-stackdump.bin` - Binary stack trace dump
- `sjk-ssa-thread-info.txt` - Per-thread summary
- `sjk-ssa-histo.txt` - Frame histogram (CSV)
- `sjk-ssa-print.txt` - Full stack traces
- `jmh-flame-graph.svg` - Flame graph visualization
- `sjk-vminfo-sysprops.txt` - System properties
- `sjk-vminfo-flags.txt` - JVM XX flags
- `sjk-mx-*.txt` - Various MBean data
- `jmh-benchmark-output.txt` - JMH benchmark output
ENDSUMMARY

=== README ===
Swiss Java Knife (SJK)
=========

SJK is a command line tool for JVM diagnostic, troubleshooting and profiling.

SJK exploits standard diagnostic interfaces of JVM (such as JMX, JVM attach and perf counters) and adds some more logic on top 
useful for common troubleshooting cases. SJK can also be used as a library for building application specific diagnostic tools
or to enhance your code with self monitoring features.

What you can do with SJK?
----

 - [Monitor Java threads in real time][ttop]
 - [Analyze head dynamics with advanced class histograms][hh]
 - [Access MBean attributes and operation from command line][mx]
 - Create [flame graphs][html-flame] and over reports from snapshots created VisualVM, Java Flight Recorder or [SJK's own sampler][stcap]
 
See [full command reference](sjk-core/COMMANDS.md).

Download
----

Latest prebuild binaries [![Last Version](https://img.shields.io/maven-central/v/org.gridkit.jvmtool/sjk.svg)](https://search.maven.org/#search%7Cga%7C1%7Cg%3A%22org.gridkit.jvmtool%22)
- `wget https://training.ragozin.info/sjk.jar` -> [sjk.jar](https://search.maven.org/remotecontent?filepath=org/gridkit/jvmtool/sjk-plus/0.22/sjk-plus-0.22.jar) 

Starting sjk
----

    java -jar sjk.jar <cmd> <arguments>
    java -jar sjk.jar --commands
    java -jar sjk.jar --help <cmd>

Below a few command from SJK ([full command reference](sjk-core/COMMANDS.md)).

[ttop]
----

Pools thread CPU usage of the target JVM and periodically reports to the console.

 - can attach via PID or open JMX port
 - displays thread memory allocation rate and cumulative process allocation rate
 - displays safe point time consumption (only if attache via PID)

[More details][ttop]

[hh]
----

Similar to `jmap -histo`.

 - plus can show a histogram of dead objects (histograms of all and live requested, then difference is calculated)
 - plus can show N top buckets in histogram

[More details][hh]

[stcap], [stcpy], [ssa] and [flame]
----

These commands provide basic sample profiler capabilities. `stcap` produces hyper-dense stack trace dump 
(about 1000 compression rate compared to text format) and `ssa` provides few reports over dump files.
`stcpy` can copy data in archives produced by `stcap` (e.g. merging dumps or filtering selected threads).

So far following reports are available:

 - [sophisticated filtering] (time, stack trace, thread name)
 - stack frame histogram with advanced filtering options
 - flame graph visualization (SVG or [interactive HTML][html-flame])
 - per thread summary (CPU usage, memory allocation, etc)

=== README ===
Swiss Java Knife (SJK)
=========

SJK is a command line tool for JVM diagnostic, troubleshooting and profiling.

SJK exploits standard diagnostic interfaces of JVM (such as JMX, JVM attach and perf counters) and adds some more logic on top 
useful for common troubleshooting cases. SJK can also be used as a library for building application specific diagnostic tools
or to enhance your code with self monitoring features.

What you can do with SJK?
----

 - [Monitor Java threads in real time][ttop]
 - [Analyze head dynamics with advanced class histograms][hh]
 - [Access MBean attributes and operation from command line][mx]
 - Create [flame graphs][html-flame] and over reports from snapshots created VisualVM, Java Flight Recorder or [SJK's own sampler][stcap]
 
See [full command reference](sjk-core/COMMANDS.md).

Download
----

Latest prebuild binaries [![Last Version](https://img.shields.io/maven-central/v/org.gridkit.jvmtool/sjk.svg)](https://search.maven.org/#search%7Cga%7C1%7Cg%3A%22org.gridkit.jvmtool%22)
- `wget https://training.ragozin.info/sjk.jar` -> [sjk.jar](https://search.maven.org/remotecontent?filepath=org/gridkit/jvmtool/sjk-plus/0.22/sjk-plus-0.22.jar) 

Starting sjk
----

    java -jar sjk.jar <cmd> <arguments>
    java -jar sjk.jar --commands
    java -jar sjk.jar --help <cmd>

Below a few command from SJK ([full command reference](sjk-core/COMMANDS.md)).

[ttop]
----

Pools thread CPU usage of the target JVM and periodically reports to the console.

 - can attach via PID or open JMX port
 - displays thread memory allocation rate and cumulative process allocation rate
 - displays safe point time consumption (only if attache via PID)

[More details][ttop]

[hh]
----

Similar to `jmap -histo`.

 - plus can show a histogram of dead objects (histograms of all and live requested, then difference is calculated)
 - plus can show N top buckets in histogram

[More details][hh]

[stcap], [stcpy], [ssa] and [flame]
----

These commands provide basic sample profiler capabilities. `stcap` produces hyper-dense stack trace dump 
(about 1000 compression rate compared to text format) and `ssa` provides few reports over dump files.
`stcpy` can copy data in archives produced by `stcap` (e.g. merging dumps or filtering selected threads).

So far following reports are available:

 - [sophisticated filtering] (time, stack trace, thread name)
 - stack frame histogram with advanced filtering options
 - flame graph visualization (SVG or [interactive HTML][html-flame])
 - per thread summary (CPU usage, memory allocation, etc)
 - converting back to text format

Dump file can be also processed programatically.

[More details][ssa]

[mx]

 - connect to local JVM processes by PID (e.i. any Java process, you do not need to enable JMX server)
 - connect to JMX using host:port (password authentication is supported)

[More details][mx]

[jps]
----

- plus can display values of specific -XX for HotSpot JVM processes 
- plus can filter process java processes by their system properties

tool_calls.command:
SJK_JAR="/workspace/jvm-tools/sjk-plus/target/sjk-plus-0.24-SNAPSHOT.jar"
TARGET_PID=14401
echo "===== SJK MX - GC Collection Count and Time ====="
java -jar "$SJK_JAR" mx -p $TARGET_PID -b "java.lang:name=G1 Young Generation,type=GarbageCollector" -f "CollectionCount,CollectionTime" -mg 2>&1 > /analysis-results/sjk-mx-gc-young.txt
cat /analysis-results/sjk-mx-gc-young.txt
echo ""
java -jar "$SJK_JAR" mx -p $TARGET_PID -b "java.lang:name=G1 Old Generation,type=GarbageCollector" -f "CollectionCount,CollectionTime" -mg 2>&1 > /analysis-results/sjk-mx-gc-old.txt
cat /analysis-results/sjk-mx-gc-old.txt
echo ""
echo "===== SJK MX - Memory Pool info ====="
java -jar "$SJK_JAR" mx -p $TARGET_PID -b "java.lang:type=MemoryPool,name=*" -mi -all 2>&1 > /analysis-results/sjk-mx-memory-pools.txt
cat /analysis-results/sjk-mx-memory-pools.txt

function.arguments:
{"command": "# Let's also run ttop output to a file and create a comprehensive summary
SJK_JAR="/workspace/jvm-tools/sjk-plus/target/sjk-plus-0.24-SNAPSHOT.jar"
TARGET_PID=14401
echo "===== SJK TTOP (saved to file) ====="
timeout 20 java -jar "$SJK_JAR" ttop -p $TARGET_PID -n 20 2>&1 > /analysis-results/sjk-ttop-output.txt
cat /analysis-results/sjk-ttop-output.txt | head -80
echo ""
echo "===== Checking JMH benchmark still running ====="
ps aux | grep java | grep -v grep | grep -v defunct | head -5"}

echo ""
echo "===== Create comprehensive analysis summary ====="
cat > /analysis-results/ANALYSIS-SUMMARY.md << 'ENDSUMMARY'
# JVM-Tools (SJK) Analysis of JMH Project

## Overview
This document summarizes the analysis of the **JMH (Java Microbenchmark Harness)** project using **jvm-tools (SJK - Swiss Java Knife)**.

## Tools Used
- **jvm-tools (SJK)**: Built from https://github.com/aragozin/jvm-tools (version 0.24-SNAPSHOT)
- **JMH**: Built from https://github.com/openjdk/jmh (version 1.38-SNAPSHOT)

## Analysis Methodology
1. Built jvm-tools from source using Maven (with toolchain disabled for JDK 17 compatibility)
2. Built JMH project from source using Maven
3. Launched a JMH benchmark (BlackholeBench.explicit_int) with 4 threads, 1000 iterations of 30s each
4. Attached SJK to the forked JMH benchmark process (PID 14401) using JVM attach mechanism
5. Collected multiple types of diagnostic data

## SJK Commands Run on JMH Process

### 1. jps - Java Process Listing
- Listed all JVM processes on the system
- Identified JMH parent process and forked benchmark process

### 2. ttop - Thread Top (CPU monitoring)
- **Key finding**: 4 JMH worker threads each consuming ~100% CPU
- Total process CPU: ~407% (4 cores fully utilized)
- Worker threads: `org.openjdk.jmh.benchmarks.BlackholeBench.explicit_int-jmh-worker-{1,2,3,4}`
- Allocation rate: 0 b/s to ~600kb/s per worker (compiler blackhole mode)

### 3. hh - Heap Histogram
- Showed JMH infrastructure objects in heap
- Key objects: Blackhole, ThreadParams, InfraControl, BenchmarkParams
- Total of ~60+ JMH-related object types

### 4. gc - GC Information
- G1 Young Generation: 2 collections, 25ms total
- G1 Old Generation: 0 collections
- Very low GC pressure (benchmark uses compiler blackholes)

### 5. stcap - Stack Trace Capture
- Captured 210 stack trace samples at 10ms intervals
- Stored in binary format for analysis

### 6. ssa - Stack Sample Analyzer
- **Thread Info**: 15 threads, 4 JMH workers at ~75% CPU each
- **Frame Histogram**: Most frequent frames are in JMH benchmark stub methods
- **Print**: Full stack traces showing JMH execution path
- **Flame Graph**: Generated SVG flame graph visualization

### 7. vminfo - VM Information
- **System Properties**: JDK 17.0.19, OpenJDK 64-Bit Server VM
- **XX Flags**: Full list of JVM flags (G1GC, tiered compilation, etc.)
- **Perf Counters**: Not available due to module access restrictions on JDK 17

### 8. mx - MBean Operations
- **Memory**: Heap usage 100MB used / 2GB committed / 30GB max
- **Threading**: 21-30 active threads
- **Runtime**: JVM arguments showing JMH-specific flags
- **GC**: G1 Young (2 collections, 25ms), G1 Old (0 collections)
- **ClassLoading**: 2379 loaded classes, 0 unloaded
- **Compilation**: 4229ms total compilation time
- **OS**: 288 available processors, low CPU load

## Key Findings
1. JMH benchmark efficiently utilizes all 4 worker threads at ~100% CPU each
2. Minimal GC pressure with G1GC - only 2 young generation collections
3. Stack traces show the benchmark execution path through JMH infrastructure
4. Heap is well under capacity with only ~100MB used
5. The benchmark uses compiler blackholes to prevent dead code elimination

## Output Files
- `sjk-ttop-output.txt` - Thread CPU monitoring data
- `sjk-hh-output.txt` - Heap histogram
- `sjk-gc-output.txt` - GC information
- `sjk-stcap-output.txt` - Stack capture log
- `jmh-stackdump.bin` - Binary stack trace dump
- `sjk-ssa-thread-info.txt` - Per-thread summary
- `sjk-ssa-histo.txt` - Frame histogram (CSV)
- `sjk-ssa-print.txt` - Full stack traces
- `jmh-flame-graph.svg` - Flame graph visualization
- `sjk-vminfo-sysprops.txt` - System properties
- `sjk-vminfo-flags.txt` - JVM XX flags
- `sjk-mx-*.txt` - Various MBean data
- `jmh-benchmark-output.txt` - JMH benchmark output
ENDSUMMARY
echo "Summary created"
echo ""
echo "===== All analysis result files ====="
ls -la /analysis-results/"}

# JVM-Tools (SJK) Analysis of JMH Project

## Overview
This document summarizes the analysis of the **JMH (Java Microbenchmark Harness)** project using **jvm-tools (SJK - Swiss Java Knife)**.

## Tools Used
- **jvm-tools (SJK)**: Built from https://github.com/aragozin/jvm-tools (version 0.24-SNAPSHOT)
- **JMH**: Built from https://github.com/openjdk/jmh (version 1.38-SNAPSHOT)

## Analysis Methodology
1. Built jvm-tools from source using Maven (with toolchain disabled for JDK 17 compatibility)
2. Built JMH project from source using Maven
3. Launched a JMH benchmark (BlackholeBench.explicit_int) with 4 threads, 1000 iterations of 30s each
4. Attached SJK to the forked JMH benchmark process (PID 14401) using JVM attach mechanism
5. Collected multiple types of diagnostic data

## SJK Commands Run on JMH Process

### 1. jps - Java Process Listing
- Listed all JVM processes on the system
- Identified JMH parent process and forked benchmark process

### 2. ttop - Thread Top (CPU monitoring)
- **Key finding**: 4 JMH worker threads each consuming ~100% CPU
- Total process CPU: ~407% (4 cores fully utilized)
- Worker threads: `org.openjdk.jmh.benchmarks.BlackholeBench.explicit_int-jmh-worker-{1,2,3,4}`
- Allocation rate: 0 b/s to ~600kb/s per worker (compiler blackhole mode)

### 3. hh - Heap Histogram
- Showed JMH infrastructure objects in heap
- Key objects: Blackhole, ThreadParams, InfraControl, BenchmarkParams
- Total of ~60+ JMH-related object types

### 4. gc - GC Information
- G1 Young Generation: 2 collections, 25ms total
- G1 Old Generation: 0 collections
- Very low GC pressure (benchmark uses compiler blackholes)

### 5. stcap - Stack Trace Capture
- Captured 210 stack trace samples at 10ms intervals
- Stored in binary format for analysis

### 6. ssa - Stack Sample Analyzer
- **Thread Info**: 15 threads, 4 JMH workers at ~75% CPU each
- **Frame Histogram**: Most frequent frames are in JMH benchmark stub methods
- **Print**: Full stack traces showing JMH execution path
- **Flame Graph**: Generated SVG flame graph visualization

### 7. vminfo - VM Information
- **System Properties**: JDK 17.0.19, OpenJDK 64-Bit Server VM
- **XX Flags**: Full list of JVM flags (G1GC, tiered compilation, etc.)
- **Perf Counters**: Not available due to module access restrictions on JDK 17
